items.fact: k-means: alternate assign / recompute; minimises within-cluster variance

Hierarchical: agglomerative merging by linkage single/complete/average/Ward; cut dendrogram
Hierarchical: O(n^2); linkage choice changes results

items.fact: DBSCAN: density-based, arbitrary shapes, outliers as noise
DBSCAN: eps/min_samples tuning; struggles with varying density
GMM + EM: soft clustering, responsibilities (E), parameter updates (M)
GMM: local optima; k still needed
Anomaly detection: isolation forest (few random splits), one-class SVM, density/reconstruction thresholds
Anomaly detection: evaluate with PR metrics, labels rare
PCA: top eigenvectors of covariance (equivalently SVD); maximal retained variance
PCA: linear only; standardise features first
t-SNE/UMAP: neighbour-preserving nonlinear embeddings for visualisation
t-SNE/UMAP: distances/cluster sizes in the plot not meaningful
UMAP faster and preserves more global structure

items.fact: Decision tree: greedy recursive splits maximising Gini/entropy reduction or variance reduction
Decision tree: interpretable; alone high variance, easy to overfit
Random forest: bootstrap samples, random feature subset per split, average/vote
Random forest: variance reduction via decorrelated trees; nearly tuning-free; OOB error free

items.fact: Gradient boosting: trees sequential, each fits gradient of loss (residuals for MSE)
XGBoost adds second-order (Hessian) info in split objective
XGBoost prefers twice-differentiable losses like log-cosh over Huber
